annotation.support_acceptance_reference: Owner visual review and crop/mask approval, 2026-09-06 session, this conversation
annotation.notes: Third ff47-event subject (blue wig, lip piercing). Two deliberate deviations from the task brief, both evidence-driven: (1) the 'mole/beauty mark' is a PAINTED heart glyph, so it is logged as makeup_edge_regions rather than protected_identity_marks; (2) noise_regions is NOT empty here -- this frame is genuinely grainy (smallest face, highest effective ISO of the batch) and labelling observed noise is not fabrication. This is the corpus's first noise/nuisance control label.
annotation.uncertainty: Examined at 8x nearest-neighbour magnification on the NATIVE crop (X, not S). Finger, mouth, piercings and wig were excluded from allow by rectangle; the finger boundary in particular is a coarse approximation. Face is only 420 px so a 512 crop necessarily spans the whole face, and the eligible skin fraction is low by construction.

makeup_edge_regions.notes: Small red PAINTED heart-shaped mark under the eye, adjacent to a pointing finger. At 8x this is a drawn/applied cosmetic glyph with a wet-paint edge and a specular highlight, NOT a natural mole or beauty mark -- the task brief's 'small mole/beauty mark near mouth corner' description does not match the pixels. Classified as an applied makeup edge accordingly.

noise_regions.notes: Dominant local signal is sensor/ISO luma+chroma grain, not skin structure: highpass_std 3.10 with lapvar 83 over a tonally flat cheek, visible as random per-pixel chroma mottling at 8x. Smallest face in the batch (420 px), so the grain is at the same spatial scale a texture arm would treat as pore detail.

uncertainty_regions.notes: Cannot separate a possible pore field from the ISO grain at this magnification; the two occupy the same spatial frequency here. Recorded as unlabelABLE rather than assigned to either category.
